SATOM 1.3.1

Rebuilt offline bundles, factory settings that no longer point at someone else's network, a new manual for the device APIs, and the documentation published in one place only.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • In short
  • What's new
  • Device APIs and the endpoint registry: a new manual
  • The manual from the operator console
  • The reading map is published
  • What changes for you
  • Fixed
  • Under the hood
  • Learn more

Released: 2026-08-03 · All releases

In short#

The offline bundles shipped with 1.3 were built before several fixes went in. On an unattended install they tried to download SATOM from a private server and hung. This release rebuilds all three bundles (Debian 12, RHEL 9 and openSUSE 15). It also:

  • removes factory settings that named one company's own network
  • tightens what the public code mirror publishes
  • adds a manual for the device APIs
  • publishes the documentation in one place only: the public site, with an offline copy in the operator console

What's new#

Device APIs and the endpoint registry: a new manual#

A new manual, Device APIs & the endpoint registry, describes how SATOM talks to your appliances. It covers:

  • The consoles. The three API consoles SATOM uses to drive an appliance.
  • The catalog behind them. 826 entries: 507 for FortiWeb, 255 for FortiADC and 64 for FortiAnalyzer.
  • Your corrections survive updates. A fix you make to an entry stays in place through every update.
  • Access. The four permissions involved, and how ADOMs limit what you see.
  • Firmware changes. If a firmware upgrade moves an API address, you edit one entry in the browser; you do not need a new SATOM release.

The manual from the operator console#

satom show docs shows the manual straight from the node, with no network. A management network usually has no route to the public site, so this keeps the manual readable offline. New documents appear in the list automatically.

The reading map is published#

The documentation index, which lists every document and suggests a reading path for each role, was the one document available in the application but not on the public site. It is now published too.

What changes for you#

  • The application no longer serves its own copy of the documentation. The in-app documentation pages are removed and now answer "not found". The sign-in page and the sidebar link to the public documentation site instead. On a node with no route to that site, use satom show docs. The staging copy of the documentation site was retired too, so there is now only one published copy.
  • Trusted proxies now default to the local machine only. The old default named another network's proxy address. Elsewhere, that made every user share one rate-limiting bucket. On a network whose addresses overlapped it, an unrelated machine could have faked the client address used for rate limiting and the audit trail.
  • The DNS Lookup tool no longer comes with preset DNS servers. The old defaults named another network's internal servers. Add your own.
  • Node certificates no longer add a fixed domain name. You can configure only the domain suffix, and SATOM works it out for each node. On an HA pair the standby therefore never issues a certificate that names the primary.
  • The installer downloads from the public repository by default, so an unattended install no longer hangs on a server it cannot reach.
  • No more links to an internal server. The About panel no longer links to an internal code server, and the sample web server configuration is now a generic example.

Fixed#

  • The public code mirror exposed internal details. It carried an internal network map and the names and email addresses of the people who made changes. The old filter checked file names and commit messages but not what was inside the files it kept. Publishing now removes internal identifiers from every file in the whole history, replaces every author identity, and checks its own output again. If anything is found, it stops and publishes nothing.
  • 71 links in the published manual were broken. Links between documents now point at the published pages, and links to documents that are not published become plain text.
  • Long pages of the published manual were blank. Every documentation page faded in as you scrolled, but pages longer than about eight screens could never trigger it and stayed invisible. Most of the manual looked empty. Content is now visible by default, and the animation only runs when the page's script has actually loaded.
  • The engineering notes left out the FortiAnalyzer catalog and still described an editor page that had been merged into the API console.
  • The published manual's callout no longer points at the removed in-app documentation. It points at satom show docs instead.

Under the hood#

  • Test data no longer uses real-looking network addresses. It now uses addresses reserved for documentation.
  • Two lab helper scripts are no longer published. They only worked against one specific lab.
